payload.name: O on Cu(111)
payload.structure_source: ASE fcc111 slab built from MACE-MP-0-relaxed fcc Cu lattice constant
payload.rationale: Task request: adsorption energy of atomic O on Cu(111) at most stable site, referenced to isolated O atom.

_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the adsorption energy of atomic oxygen on Cu(111) at its most stable site, referenced to an isolated O atom.

summary: candidate O on Cu(111) (adsorbate_on_metal_surface, trust tier)

method.model: MACE-MP-0 medium (2023-12-03, trained on MPtrj PBE/PBE+U)
method.protocol: 0 K static relaxations (BFGS, fmax 0.01 eV/A). Bulk fcc Cu relaxed with cell filter -> a = 3.626 A. Cu(111) slab 3x3 in-plane, 5 layers, 8 A vacuum each side (16 A gap), bottom 2 layers fixed. O placed at fcc, hcp, ontop, bridge and relaxed (bridge relaxes into fcc). E_ads = E(slab+O) - E(slab) - E(O atom); E(O atom) = MACE energy of a single O in a 15 A box (non-spin-polarized model, so this is the model's isolated-atom baseline). Most stable site is fcc hollow. Convergence checks: 2x2x4 (0.25 ML) -4.428, 3x3x4 -4.436, 3x3x5 -4.436 eV.

payload.note: Most stable site is the fcc hollow at 1/9 ML: E_ads = -4.44 eV vs isolated O atom. hcp is 0.014 eV less stable (-4.42), which is below what this model can resolve. Ontop gives -2.54 eV. O sits 1.13 A above the surface plane. Referenced to 1/2 O2 with the same model, E_ads = -1.67 eV. PREMISE ISSUE: an MLIP trained on condensed-phase PBE data does not describe a spin-polarized free O atom. Its isolated-atom energy is a fitted baseline (E0), so the atom-referenced number carries a reference error the model cannot fix. This is why the result is flagged. VALIDATION with the same model and settings: (1) Cu lattice constant 3.626 A vs experiment about 3.615 A (+0.3%), passes. (2) Isolated-atom-referenced quantities fail. The Cu cohesive energy is 3.16 eV vs experiment 3.49 eV (Kittel, Introduction to Solid State Physics), so it is underbound by 0.33 eV. The O2 binding energy is 5.53 eV vs experiment De about 5.21 eV (D0 = 5.12 eV, Huber & Herzberg) and vs PBE about 6.0-6.2 eV, so the model matches neither. (3) A literature PBE value from a web search (arXiv:2505.12914, VASP-PBE, isolated gas-phase O reference) gives fcc -5.00 / hcp -4.91 eV; I could not confirm that paper's coverage. MACE is about 0.56 eV weaker than this, and its fcc > hcp ordering agrees. ALTERNATIVE (well-posed) estimate: model E_ads vs 1/2 O2 (-1.67 eV) minus half the experimental O2 De (2.61 eV) gives -4.28 eV. UNCERTAINTY +/-0.6 eV covers the spread across the MACE value, this alternative and the PBE literature value, plus the isolated-atom reference error (0.3-0.6 eV). Finite size and slab thickness contribute <0.01 eV; the fcc/hcp ordering contributes 0.014 eV. Not included: the spread across DFT functionals (PBE is known to overbind O on metals; RPBE is weaker by several tenths of an eV), zero-point energy (about 0.05-0.07 eV), thermal effects and coverage beyond 0.25 ML. No experimental atom-referenced value was used or claimed.
